name: Instant air refreshment sprays (aerosol cans, trigger sprays)
anchor: route-scoped sovereign inhaled-product content maxima. Lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury read across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division 2022 route table for "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray" (500 / 200 / 200 / 100 ug/kg), corroborated at identical values by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products; total chromium reads across from the Maryland Cannabis Administration inhalation-route value (600 ug/kg) and is published as a screen. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it is a component prohibition on the metal of a wick core and is carried on the scented-candles row as an independent regulatory hard stop, never as a finished-article ceiling. Nickel, tin, aluminium, inorganic arsenic and hexavalent chromium are held under mandatory control because no government sets a content maximum for them in any inhaled consumer product.
native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. A manual actuation aerosolises a hydroalcoholic or oil-in-water fragrance concentrate directly into room air. Essentially the whole dispensed mass enters the breathing zone within seconds as an inspirable or respirable aerosol, which makes this the most direct product-to-lung transfer in the category and the form closest in mechanism to the metered-dose nasal spray that Colorado's inhalation row names. SCOPE. In scope: hand-held aerosol cans, bag-on-valve units, compressed-gas cans, and non-propellant trigger and pump sprays sold to refresh room air. Out of scope: fabric and textile refresher sprays whose primary claim is deposition on a surface rather than emission into air, disinfectant and biocidal sprays, personal body mists and fine fragrance (Category 13 or 14 by the leave-on cosmetic route), and insecticidal aerosols. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the fragrance concentrate; the solvent and carrier phase (ethanol, water, glycols); the liquefied or compressed propellant; the tinplate or aluminium aerosol can and its internal lacquer; the valve cup, stem, gasket and dip tube; the actuator and any nickel-plated or chrome-plated trim; and any added colorant. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this form aerosolises its charge mechanically, essentially the whole non-volatile content of the dispensed mass is delivered to the breathing zone rather than left behind, so the content screen on the charge is the closest available proxy for what is inhaled and the wetted dispense path is sampled as a separate component. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
material: the filled aerosol formulation as dispensed (fragrance concentrate, solvent and carrier phase, and liquefied or compressed propellant), presented in a tinplate or aluminium can with a metering or continuous valve
components: The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the fragrance concentrate; the solvent and carrier phase (ethanol, water, glycols); the liquefied or compressed propellant; the tinplate or aluminium aerosol can and its internal lacquer; the valve cup, stem, gasket and dip tube; the actuator and any nickel-plated or chrome-plated trim; and any added colorant. Every listed component is sampled and tested as a distinct component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, and hexavalent-chromium reflex speciation on a component follows the reference method published on this row's Cr-VI cell. EMISSION PATH. The components in the emission path, which branch (b) of every numeric cell's disposition governs, are the can's internal lacquer, the valve cup, stem, gasket and dip tube, and the actuator nozzle, every one of which the formulation wets or passes through on its way into the air. Every component result carries a criterion and a lot consequence under the three ordered branches published on each numeric cell: a sovereign instrument that reaches the component and the analyte governs it in its own basis and an exceedance blocks certification; an emission-path component is governed through the published value applied to emitting material sampled from the finished assembled article; and any remaining component result is held to ALARA against demonstrated process capability, with CAPA, raw-material traceback and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No component ceiling is invented.
basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: as sold, ug of element per kg of the emitting material (product as tested)
Pb.source_scope: inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray
Pb.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
Pb.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the filled formulation as dispensed, including propellant by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires one analysis beyond the published test, and it carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a tinplate or aluminium aerosol can, a nickel-plated or chrome-plated actuator trim, a valve cup or a pigmented moulded housing is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. For lead and this row's components, branch (a) is EMPTY, and the instruments checked before saying so are named rather than waved at: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU is scoped to the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment and this row carries no powered sub-assembly; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries is scoped to batteries and this row contains none; REACH Annex XVII entry 63 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/628 (eu_2015_628_pb_mouthable_general_public_articles_0_05pct) reaches only articles supplied to the general public that may be placed in the mouth by children; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 reaches consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles and does not reach a packaging, sachet or decorative textile that is not worn; the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, the CPSIA surface-coating limit and the Canadian and Australian toy-coating limits reach accessible toy material and toy surface coatings, and none of these articles is a toy; 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) reaches only the metal of a candlewick core and this row has no wick core; the food-contact ceramic, glassware and enamelware instruments reach only articles intended to come into contact with food. Every component result on this row therefore falls to branch (b) or branch (c), and neither leaves a result without a criterion or without a lot consequence. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the can's internal lacquer, the valve cup, stem, gasket and dip tube, and the actuator nozzle, every one of which the formulation wets or passes through on its way into the air), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life or after the declared maximum number of actuations, whichever is the more demanding, so that any lead transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for lead, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the fragrance house, the solvent and propellant supplier, the can and internal-lacquer maker, the valve maker and the actuator moulder; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a lead content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one.

iAs.rationale: No government sets an inorganic-arsenic content maximum for any inhaled consumer product or any home-air product. Every route-scoped inhaled-product instrument regulates arsenic as the unspeciated total: Colorado, California, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada and Israel all publish total arsenic and none of them speciates, so there is no inorganic-arsenic cell anywhere to read across from. The article and component instruments checked were EU RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Annex II (lead, cadmium, total mercury and hexavalent chromium in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment), the EU Batteries Regulation Annex I (mercury, cadmium and lead in batteries), REACH Annex XVII entry 23 (cadmium in synthetic polymers, paint and painted articles), REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin expressed as tin in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public), REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and hexavalent chromium in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles), REACH Annex XVII entry 63 paragraph 7 (lead in mouthable articles), Canada SOR/2016-193 (lead and mercury in surface coating materials), Canada SOR/2018-83 (lead in accessible parts of children's products), Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892 (lead and cadmium in listed covered consumer products), and the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 with EN 71-3 (element migration from toy materials). Every one of them governs a component of an article in a different basis, and none of them is a content maximum for the material a home-air product puts into the breathing zone. The cosmetic content instruments checked and rejected on route were Germany BVL 2017 (technically avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics), Health Canada's cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive contaminant guideline v3 (2019), Korea MFDS 2025-63 and 2024-9, China's 2015 Cosmetics Safety and Technical Standards, India's Cosmetics Rules 2020, Indonesia BPOM 16/2024, Malaysia NPRA, the New Zealand Cosmetic Products Group Standard, Kenya KS 2937:2021, Taiwan's 2024 prohibited-ingredient residual limits, EAEU TR CU 009/2011, and the Hong Kong Mercury Control Ordinance cosmetics provision. All of them are content limits for products applied to the human body on a dermal or mucosal basis. A home-air product is not applied to the body, so none of them is route-applicable. A NOT-MATERIAL determination is deliberately rejected rather than adopted for convenience, because inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction and it is genuinely material in this row. Inorganic arsenic is material here through mineral-derived colorants and any clay- or silicate-derived opacifier or suspending agent in the formulation. The cell is therefore a control: testing is mandatory, the species is bounded by identity below the published total-arsenic ceiling of 200 ug/kg, and no number is invented. No occupational exposure limit, indoor-air guideline or ambient-air standard was used, and none was converted into a product ceiling: an air concentration is not a product content maximum and HMTc does not manufacture one from the other.
iAs.reference_method: Total arsenic on every certified lot of the filled formulation as dispensed, including propellant by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the ArCl interference. Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by anion-exchange HPLC-ICP-MS is ordered whenever the total-arsenic screen reaches half the published total-arsenic ceiling (100 ug/kg), and unconditionally on the first lot from any new supplier of mineral filler, pigment, glaze, frit, clay, charcoal, joss powder, hydrocolloid or dried botanical material. Component-level sampling covers the fragrance concentrate; the solvent and carrier phase (ethanol, water, glycols); the liquefied or compressed propellant; the tinplate or aluminium aerosol can and its internal lacquer; the valve cup, stem, gasket and dip tube; the actuator and any nickel-plated or chrome-plated trim; and any added colorant. The wetted dispense path (valve, stem, dip tube, nozzle, mesh and reservoir) is rinsed and the rinsate analysed as a separate component, because that path is in the aerosol stream. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic sediment and biomagnifies through aquatic food webs. This row's emitting material is a manufactured non-marine formulation (the filled formulation as dispensed, including propellant) with no methylation pathway, no aquatic trophic transfer and no marine-derived or wild-harvested animal input, and methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so MeHg is less than or equal to tHg by identity and is bounded by and controlled through the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg. Methylmercury is additionally thermally labile and decomposes well below the temperatures reached in any heated or combustion form in this category, so no thermal pathway creates it either. No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury limit for any air-care product, and no routed occurrence source reports methylmercury in one, which is the speciation-aware condition the not-material integrity gate applies. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published because none would bind below the total-mercury ceiling.
MeHg.reference_method: Not measured routinely. Bounded by the total-mercury cell, which is determined on every lot by EPA 7473 thermal decomposition/amalgamation atomic absorption or by ICP-MS after closed-vessel digestion. Methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is reflex-triggered only where a lot's total mercury reaches half the published total-mercury ceiling (50 ug/kg), or where a reformulation introduces any marine-derived, fish-derived or wild-harvested animal raw material, which would additionally require the row to be re-dispositioned from not-material to control.
